mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 falls for two straight quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months in a row.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which compresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during four-month stretches of below-trend industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over two months signals a deflationary easing, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fall for two straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) over three months indicates robust household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 and HOUST both rise for three consecutive months in an early-cycle regime.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above the prior six-month average for four consecutive months signals strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 6-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS exceeds its 6-month moving average for four straight months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, combined with a flat or declining unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates a buildup of precautionary savings without labor market stress, which can signal future consumption-driven demand and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for six months AND UNRATE <= prior month for six months
regime_hint: precautionary savings accumulation without labor slack
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for six months and UNRATE is flat or declining for the same period.
